defects_closed.defect: PKCS7_dataInit read the cipher-reported IV and key lengths and wrote them into fixed [u8; 16] / [u8; 64] stack buffers through RAND_bytes_ex and EVP_CIPHER_CTX_rand_key.
defects_closed.fix: Refuse ivlen > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH and keylen > EVP_MAX_KEY_LENGTH with PKCS7_DOIT_CIPHER_LENGTH_REFUSED before either write; every length that fits keeps the authority's control flow.
defects_closed.class: UB in the C authority not reproduced (AGENTS.md section 17); reachable at the C ABI, not from parsed PKCS#7 alone.

defects_closed.defect: Twelve PKCS7_dataInit failure paths leaked an already-built BIO filter chain: the digest chain was a bare pointer released only on the single success-adjacent tail, and the cipher filter was released alone.
defects_closed.fix: OwnedChain (Drop = BIO_free_all) owns the chain under construction and a second owner holds the cipher filter until the success path links it; BIO_free_all expressions in PKCS7_dataInit went 8 -> 0.
defects_closed.class: ownership reconstruction; leak paths eliminated.

defects_closed.defect: CMS_add0_recipient_password wrote a cipher-reported IV length into a fixed [u8; 16] buffer through RAND_bytes_ex and then handed it to EVP_EncryptInit_ex.
defects_closed.fix: Refuse ivlen > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH with CMS_PWRI_IV_REFUSED before the write; reachable at the C ABI through a METH/provider cipher, not from parsed DER alone.
defects_closed.class: UB in the C authority not reproduced (AGENTS.md section 17).

defects_closed.defect: kek_wrap_key read in[0..3] as the RFC 3211 header without proving three bytes were readable; with a block size of 1-4 and a 0-2 byte input the length checks did not imply inlen >= 3.
defects_closed.fix: Refuse inlen < 3 before the round-up and before any pointer use; use checked_add/checked_mul for the round-up and refuse a non-positive block size before casting.
defects_closed.class: internal-boundary out-of-bounds read; C-ABI reachable with a custom KEK cipher and a short content key.

defects_closed.defect: tls13_psk_do_binder read hashsize bytes through a bare *const u8 supplied from an attacker-length ClientHello binder, so a valid ticket with a 1-byte binder caused an out-of-bounds read.
defects_closed.fix: The received binder is a &[u8] and the compare requires received.len() == hashsize; the caller also refuses a resolved-ticket binder of the wrong length with the authority's DECODE_ERROR/BAD_EXTENSION and bounds the transcript offset.
defects_closed.class: attacker-reachable out-of-bounds read from the wire; fixed.

defects_closed.defect: The ClientHello extension walk published SNI, ALPN, status type, PHA and peer sigalgs as each extension was reached, so a later malformed extension left partial state published on a rejected hello; truncations were silently accepted and lengths were computed by hand.
defects_closed.fix: A two-pass safe parse over &[u8] returns Result<ParsedExtensions, HelloReject> and never touches Ssl; one unsafe commit_client_hello publishes only after the whole block and callback succeed; every reject goes through one ossl_statem_fatal closure that poisons the state machine with the authority's alert/reason. 15 malformed cases covered.
defects_closed.class: state-preservation and unchecked-length elimination; OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

defects_closed.defect: SSL_CTX_add_session's eviction arm invoked the application removal callback while holding ctx.lock; the crate's CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock reports recursive acquisition as failure, so a callback that re-entered the cache silently failed.
defects_closed.fix: Detach every entry, unlock, then invoke the removal callback and release the detached reference outside the lock; the callback is snapshotted so a retiring context is not re-read.
defects_closed.class: reentrancy edge (AGENTS.md section 21); deliberate safety divergence from the authority's lock-held callback.

defects_closed.defect: Insert evicted size-cap entries before the push that could refuse, so a refused push removed live entries and was not failure-atomic; the replacement arm released the incumbent before the push.
defects_closed.fix: Push first, then replace the incumbent and evict down to session_cache_size; a refused push returns 0 with the cache unchanged.
defects_closed.class: failure atomicity.

defects_closed.defect: Last-reference releases (application ex_data destructors) ran under ctx.lock for both the replaced incumbent and each evicted entry.
defects_closed.fix: Release every detached cache reference after unlock.
defects_closed.class: reentrancy edge (ex_data callback under a non-recursive lock).

defects_closed.defect: SSL_SESS_CACHE_UPDATE_TIME was applied only to new entries, so re-adding a cached session did not refresh its expiry as the authority does.
defects_closed.fix: Update time and recalculate the timeout unconditionally after the same-key decision.
defects_closed.class: compatibility.

defects_closed.defect: A negative SSL_CTX_flush_sessions cutoff was cast to u64 and flushed the entire cache; the authority's signed comparison expires nothing for t < 0.
defects_closed.fix: Compare the signed cutoff so only t == 0 flushes everything.
defects_closed.class: compatibility.

defects_closed.defect: The authority's every-255-connections automatic cache flush was not modelled, so a long-lived context never expired sessions automatically.
defects_closed.fix: Implement the authority trigger, counter and SSL_CTX_flush_sessions_ex call, including its no-op error behaviour.
defects_closed.class: compatibility; recorded reduction closed.

defects_closed.defect: TLS1.2 DHE client key exchange failed. Four causes: SSL_R_BAD_SIGNATURE was defined as 148 (SSL_R_DH_PUBLIC_VALUE_LENGTH_IS_WRONG) instead of 123; tls12_verify did not implement the rsa_pss_rsae/pss or DSA signature schemes; extended_master_secret was advertised but neither the server echo nor RFC 7627's session-hash master secret was implemented; and tls12_process_server_key_exchange had no SSL_kDHE arm at all.
defects_closed.fix: Implement the DHE arm with checked p/g/Ys parsing, big-endian BN import (OSSL_PARAM_construct_BN is native-endian), param/public checks, security-bits check and signature verification; add the PSS/DSA schemes and correct SSL_R_BAD_SIGNATURE to 123; record the EMS echo and derive the RFC 7627 master secret; add the DHE GCM suites.
defects_closed.class: implementation defect with an attacker-visible parity failure; the negative-control canary is an ECDHE-only reader refusing the DHE frame.

defects_closed.defect: Five typed-slice constructions were formed over caller-supplied writable output before any byte was written. The C contract promises writable storage, never initialised values, so the &mut [u8] over the whole capacity required validity the ABI does not provide. tls13_next_handshake_message was reachable with OwnedBuf::new memory (CRYPTO_malloc, uninitialised) from statem_srvr::tls13_server_drive: real UB on the TLS1.3 server path. The alert read-back could also derive a slice from a NULL buffer when n == 0.
defects_closed.fix: Keep the output as a raw writable region. Copy with core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping after a body.len() <= cap check, pass the raw pointer and capacity to the two decrypt sinks, publish a &[u8] only over the written prefix (n <= cap), and use an empty slice for the n == 0 alert. The non-overlap precondition is documented on every entry point.
defects_closed.class: ownership reconstruction of an output boundary; 5 typed-slice constructions eliminated. Graded OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED: Miri/ASan and independent review are NOT_RUN and non-overlap is not type-enforced.

defects_closed.defect: getivgen formed a &mut [u8] over the caller's output buffer, which both callers and the C authority treat as write-only; the provider ABI does not require initialised u8 values there. gcm_tls_cipher's in-place aliasing was sound (out == in_ is enforced and split_at_mut was disjoint), but its whole-record from_raw_parts_mut(out, len) required all len bytes to be initialised while the explicit-IV and tag slots are output-only on encryption (24 uninitialised bytes in the canary).
defects_closed.fix: Keep the destination/record as raw writable memory. getivgen writes olen bytes with copy_nonoverlapping and forms no reference over out. gcm_tls_cipher derives payload and tag_slot by ptr::add from the already-checked len, passes one raw payload pointer to the hardware one-shot, and keeps the authentication-failure cleanse and tag extent unchanged.
defects_closed.class: ownership reconstruction of a provider output boundary; 2 whole-extent typed-slice constructions eliminated. Graded OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED: Miri/ASan and independent review are NOT_RUN and the caller-initialisation/non-overlap conditions remain documented ABI preconditions.

defects_closed.defect: collect and find_end called check_tlen with a NULL context, so the authority's TOO_LONG pre-check was skipped and the declared content extent was never bounded before use. In collect, a declared 127-byte nested primitive with one byte remaining caused a copy that ran 126 bytes past the input; find_end also advanced over an overlong nested element before checking the distance. The raw cursor made an out-of-bounds position representable.
defects_closed.fix: Introduce Cursor (pointer + remaining) whose advance/advance_to/take/limit/read_u8 refuse to leave the input and leave the cursor unchanged on refusal; collect, find_end and check_tlen take &mut Cursor and prove every declared extent before any read. d2i_ex_primitive holds one cursor from (in_, inlen) and publishes *in_ only after the content codec succeeds. The CVE-2026-34180 class (content length near/above 2 GiB narrowing to a negative or wrapped c_int) is excluded by the checked header TOO_LONG test plus codec INT_MAX guards, with boundary tests.
defects_closed.class: ownership/representation reconstruction of the cursor and content extent; production unsafe blocks 252 -> 238. Graded OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED: Miri/ASan and independent review are NOT_RUN and the internal template call boundary still carries checked pointer arithmetic.

defects_closed.defect: legacy.so declared DT_NEEDED libcrypto.so.3 but carried no DT_RPATH/DT_RUNPATH, so in a process that had not already mapped the candidate libcrypto the loader resolved the module against the host libcrypto 3.0.22. Separately, the candidate libcrypto's compiled-in MODULESDIR is the empty sentinel (a recorded Phase-16 distribution divergence), so the provider is only discoverable when OPENSSL_MODULES is set.
defects_closed.fix: Relink legacy.so with -Wl,--enable-new-dtags -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN/..' (DT_RUNPATH, so LD_LIBRARY_PATH still overrides for ABI-SUBSTITUTION) and apply the same flag in the ASan build script. Have downstream_runtime set OPENSSL_MODULES per subject, the same prefix substitution as LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Proof: dlopen maps only the install libcrypto, legacy loads, MD4(abc) = a448017aaf21d8525fc10ae87aa6729d, medusa exit 0 matching the authority, openvpn loads the provider with a bogus-provider negative control; 11/11 ABI courts including libcrypto-contamination. libcrypto/libssl hashes are unchanged.
defects_closed.class: distribution/linkage defect; ELF search path plus a harness environment variable, with no Rust source change

defects_closed.defect: The record reader used one raw int for retry, EOF and a completed zero-length record. A completed empty handshake record was reported as -1 (a retry) and stalled assembly, and a short read could be consumed as if it carried bytes. The pre-fix test rec_layer_empty_record_before_a_message_is_not_a_retry failed with `left: -1; right: 5`.
defects_closed.fix: ReadStatus variants make the confusion unrepresentable: only Complete carries a length; WouldBlock/Fatal/Failed map to -1 and Eof/FatalEof to 0; AssemblyStep normalises rd_msg_len/rd_msg_off and skips a completed empty record under MAX_EMPTY_RECORDS.
defects_closed.class: representation/state confusion; observed failing before the fix, then passing. OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

defects_closed.defect: tls13_encrypt_record formed &mut [u8] over the caller's whole uninitialised record buffer (from_raw_parts_mut(out, out_len)) before writing it. S39 fixed the read path but this write sink still formed a typed reference over write-only caller memory.
defects_closed.fix: OutRegion keeps the region raw; writes are capacity-checked and no reference is formed over caller memory.
defects_closed.class: UB in caller-output handling; typed slice over uninitialised output eliminated.

defects_closed.defect: tls13_decrypt_record formed &mut [u8] over CRYPTO_malloc scratch for the whole plain_cap before the AEAD wrote it. The S39 receipt had called it a cleansed block, but new_cleansed is malloc, not zalloc.
defects_closed.fix: The plaintext stays a raw writable region until authentication; the slice covers only outl == ct_body_len authenticated bytes.
defects_closed.class: typed slice over uninitialised allocator memory; eliminated.

defects_closed.defect: tls13_encrypt_record accepted a short AEAD update (outl < inner_len) and still published out_len bytes, which could include an uninitialised gap in the record.
defects_closed.fix: Success now requires outl == inner_len; the tag is placed only then.
defects_closed.class: short-write acceptance; failure-atomic refusal at the output boundary.

defects_closed.defect: Collected::take_raw cleared the owner, and the block was reclaimed by an unsafe Collected::adopt only on a normal return from ex_c2i. An unwind out of ex_c2i left the block owned by nobody.
defects_closed.fix: ContentHandoff owns the block from take_raw until after ex_c2i; its Drop releases it unless the codec cleared free_cont, so normal failure, success-without-consumption and unwinding all release exactly once. Collected::adopt is removed.
defects_closed.class: partial-object ownership; unwinding leak eliminated.

defects_closed.defect: free_cont was a Rust bool whose address was cast to the prim_c2i hook's char*. A conforming C hook may store any char, after which reading the slot as bool is an invalid-value read (UB).
defects_closed.fix: The flag is c_char throughout d2i_ex_primitive, ex_c2i and ContentHandoff; any non-zero byte means the codec still owns the block. The hook receives *mut c_char with no cast through bool.
defects_closed.class: invalid-value read at a C callback edge; eliminated.

defects_closed.defect: The X.509 extension cache was written into the X509 at each decode point, so a lock-free reader could observe a half-built cache, setup_crldp installed a decoded stack before validating its points, and x509_cb released only the skid slot, leaking the other six decoded values on X509_free or re-decode.
defects_closed.fix: CacheBuild decodes and derives every value into local owned state (CacheValue<T>, one owner per slot); publish installs all seven slots and scalars under the write lock and ex_flags|EXFLAG_SET is the single publication point; the D2I_PRE and FREE_POST arms re-adopt and release every installed slot exactly once and idempotently. The lazy-CRLDP repair is preserved (no relative name expansion; dpname stays NULL).
defects_closed.class: ownership reconstruction plus a real cache-teardown leak; the invalid-certificate cache retention is the authority's deliberate state.

defects_closed.defect: lookup_sess_in_cache fabricated a whole SslSession with mem::zeroed() and compared it through a raw byte loop; its validity was a property of every current and future SSL_SESSION field, and an over-wide stored session_id_length made the authority's memcmp read past the id array.
defects_closed.fix: SessionKey holds exactly ssl_version, session_id_length and session_id, is written field-by-field, and matches() refuses a stored length wider than SSL_MAX_SSL_SESSION_ID_LENGTH instead of reading out of bounds. SessionRef gives every cache/lookup/callback reference one owner whose Drop releases it exactly once.
defects_closed.class: zeroed-storage-as-valid-T obligation eliminated; authority out-of-bounds read not reproduced (AGENTS.md section 17).

defects_closed.defect: ssl_security_default_callback answered 1 for every operation, so ssl_method_error's SSL_SECOP_VERSION check never enforced the default security level's TLS1.2 floor. With SSL_OP_NO_TLSv1 opening a hole in the version table, ssl_get_min_max_version selected SSLv3 as the maximum and commit_client_hello rejected every ClientHello with SSL_R_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL. charybdis exposed it once S60 repaired the workload fixture.
defects_closed.fix: Implement ssl_get_security_level_bits (level clamp and the authority's minbits table) and the full SSL_SECOP_VERSION arm, including DTLS ordering, the context-only VERSION answer, and the level-0 SSL_SECOP_TMP_DH refusal. The other callback arms remain permissive as recorded.
defects_closed.class: compatibility defect with a candidate-only handshake failure; repaired to documented authority behaviour, not classified as a section 17 divergence.

S49 BIO-callback non-reentrancy precondition: a custom BIO method that re-enters the connection would invalidate the `&mut Ssl`. It is now stated on every entry point (it was implicit before), matches the authority's assumption, and is not type-enforceable at the C ABI.

S50 retained: `s: *mut Ssl` liveness/exclusive ownership is the caller's C ABI contract; OutRegion::new's writable-and-non-overlapping region and the raw encrypt/decrypt/transcript input regions are boundary preconditions; transcript_hash's raw output and the Finished secret pointers remain C ABI inputs with stated extents; the digest handle must be a live EVP_MD.

S50 introduced: refusal when an AEAD update does not produce the declared ciphertext/plaintext extent, and when hs_md_len is 0 or above EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE; both are internal-state refusals, not reachable from valid records. S50 residuals S50-R1..R5: Miri/ASan/Loom, a full library suite, allocation-failure injection, type-enforcement of the raw transcript/Finished extents, and independent review are NOT_RUN.

S51 retained: C1 hdrlen + plen stays checked-at-site so an unrepresentable sum still raises TOO_LONG (1219) where the authority does; C5 Collected::append growth stays checked-at-site (authority long-overflow test plus CRYPTO_realloc); C6 ex_c2i keeps the authority's narrowing cast and per-arm guards; C7 ASN1_get_object stays checked-at-site and is proved sound by the max-accounting invariant with src/asn1/der.rs unchanged; the EXTERN d2i and prim_c2i hooks remain raw ABI edges; the S41 stale-TLC refusal remains.

S51 residuals: a panic after an ASN.1 value has been allocated but before item_ex_d2i_intern's failure free still leaks the value (pre-existing, broader than the take_raw handoff fixed here; guard_ffi catches the unwind but does not run the failure free); a caller sharing an ASN1_TLC cache across top-level calls can reuse a fitting header cached by a failed decode (authority-compatible, no memory unsafety); a failing EXTERN hook's partial *in advance is discarded (deliberate 'no progress on failure', unobservable for X509_NAME/X509_PUBKEY); the canary observes Drop, not the pre-fix leak, and Miri/ASan are NOT_RUN; ASN1_get_object does not write *plength for an indefinite length, matching the authority.
S20-O2: stale 'Phase 8'/'unreachable' site comments remain at some EVP_PKEY sites; the evp_pkey_name2type comment was corrected in S21, the rest are still open.

S22 retained items: ml_dsa Vector::init / matrix_init remain safe raw-pointer constructors; x509::pcy_lib::tree_levels retains its aliasing obligation. The provider::cipher_gcm out-buffer slice item is closed by S40.

S39 retained: the C ABI still hands raw writable memory, so pointer/extent validity and non-overlap with rec_body/rd_msg_buf are caller preconditions documented per function and not type-enforced. S39 residual: true allocation-failure injection is unavailable and Miri/ASan are NOT_RUN. S49 extends this boundary and retains the same class of caller preconditions.

S40 retained: the provider ABI cannot enforce that an encrypt caller initialised the plaintext or that a decrypt caller supplied a received record; explicit-IV/tag slots are write-only outputs and may be uninitialised. Non-overlap is a documented precondition matching the C memcpy/one-shot requirements.

S27 retained: after EVP_CIPHER_CTX_rand_key succeeds, PKCS#7 failure paths still leave key bytes on the stack; the authority has the same behaviour and the obligation is recorded, not changed. S28 retained: the pre-existing raise_cms helper records cms_lib.c for existing cms_pwri raise sites.

S29 retained: custom extensions, context-inappropriate extension rejection, status_request DER, missing supported_groups, key_share priority/HRR, psk_ke, ext_defs error order, the 32-entry supported_groups cap and the legacy_version clamp remain documented reductions or compatibility gaps. commit_client_hello remains unsafe with four caller-established preconditions. S50 makes the binder length check structural but does not discharge these.

S30 retained: insertion-order eviction/flush; capacity N rather than the authority's at-most-N-1; no not_resumable check in ssl_update_cache; lookup_sess_in_cache ignores SSL_SESS_CACHE_NO_INTERNAL_LOOKUP and the external get_session_cb; TLS1.2 NewSessionTicket remains a stateful cache lookup. Removal callbacks run outside the lock as a deliberate safety divergence.

S34 retained: the in-crate server still does not implement DHE; DHE-DSS, ffdhe3072/4096/6144/8192, custom primes and a no-EMS server were not observed; no dudect/ctgrind run was made for the DHE premaster path.

S56 residuals S56-R1..R7: XSTANDARD/XPTABLE single-threaded access remains a caller obligation (the Sync impl is conditional, not enforced); x509_vfy reads crldp/nc/altname/akid/skid/ex_flags without the cache lock, so cross-thread safety against a racing first build is NOT established; X509_set_proxy_pathlen still writes ex_pcpathlen unlocked (authority behaviour); X509::policy_cache teardown remains outside the seven cache owners; invalid-certificate cache retention is deliberate authority-compatible state; exactly-once release is asserted by a test-only thread-local audit, not an allocator transcript; the publish NULL-slot check is a debug_assert!, not the safety argument. The lazy-CRLDP repair is preserved exactly.

S57 residual: the session-cache reference lifetime is ESTABLISHED (lookup holds the context read lock across cache_find and SSL_SESSION_up_ref, and every mutator takes the write lock), but data-race freedom is NOT ESTABLISHED. Eviction/removal/flush write not_resumable and owner under the write lock while a thread that already owns a reference reads them and the session payload unlocked; that is a data race in the Rust model and formally in C, and the authority has the same structure. No lock was added that the authority does not take. The session-cache reference lifetime is established by the context lock, but not_resumable/owner and the session payload are read without a lock by a thread that already owns a reference while eviction/removal/flush write them under the write lock. That is a data race in the Rust model and formally in C, matching the authority's structure; no lock was added that the authority does not take.
